This is a review of the Supercard MiniSD, a commonly available (as of mid 2015) flash cart for Nintendo DS, DS Lite and GBA.

The tl;dr is that it's cheap and commonly available and if you have no other option it'll do, but I wouldn't suggest it overall.

I have two of these flash carts, one I bought off eBay and one off Amazon. One works very reliably and the other has a faulty card reader or something and fails to load the MiniSD card about 4 out of 5 times.

The cartridge is a clear dark purple and has the same dimensions as a normal GBA cartridge. This allows it to be used with the original GBA variants including the Gameboy Micro as well as the original DS and DS Lite. If you're using a DS Lite though, about half the cartridge will stick out just as a normal GBA cart does. One of my cartridges has a glossy slick label, the other has a slightly more matte label with a bit more texture but still obviously a decent quality label, not standard paper stock. On the back both of them have a small white circle sticker with Chinese and a number, which I assume is some kind of batch or quality control. The screw in the top center on both of them has scratches around it where they appear to have scuffed the plastic during assembly. I use the glossiness of the label and the size of the screwdriver mark to tell mine apart. The glossy label one actually works consistently.

The flash cart uses a MiniSD card, as its name implies, to load roms etc from. The MiniSD was popular in cameras and phones for an extremely brief phase between SD and MicroSD and it's pretty rare these days. It's much easier to get an adapter from MiniSD to MicroSD and use a MicroSD card instead. When I did this though, I found it would give me errors related to reading the card almost every time. Sometimes it would say there was no card, or other times it would say that it wasn't formatted correctly. The flash cart is only able to read SD (as opposed to SDHC or SDXC) cards too so you're limited to a 2GB card max. I did manage to go on eBay and get a pair of Nokia brand 2GB MiniSD cards and after formatting them with the Panasonic SD formatting tool they worked perfectly in the better flash cart but still had the same troubles in the less reliable cartridge. Using actual MiniSD though brought the less reliable cartridge from a 0% success rate to about a 20% success rate at recognizing and loading data.

If you have a DS slot one cart capable of loading DS roms from Slot 2 (not very common any more though I know the DSTwo lets you do this) then you can use the Supercard MiniSD as an actual DS flash cart and run DS roms off it. In no way do I advocate this, but it's possible. There are slot 1 (NDS cartridge slot) flash carts that work with everything from the original DS to a fully updated New 3DS and use Micro SDHC cards up to 32GB with no adapter, so it just makes no sense to use the Supercard MiniSD for DS roms in my opinion.

With nothing in slot 1 though, the DS and DS Lite will run the Supercard MiniSD as a GBA cart. If you just put the flash cart in a GBA, it will run as a GBA cart. Really, this is where it's useful. You can store a lot of GBA games in 2GB of space and switch between them easily. On boot you'll be presented with a menu allowing you to select the games you have stored on the MiniSD card. Choose one, you'll see a quick progress indicator as it loads it to memory, and then you're playing.

The cartridge requires you to use a special software to patch the roms you put on the MiniSD card. It'll load and run the games fine without doing this but you won't have access to certain hotkey combinations while playing. You need to have these available if you want to save. During gameplay the flash cart will not overwrite your rom's save data without you explicitly telling it to. Consequently you can save in game all you want, but until you use the flash cart's save hotkey and tell it to write to the MiniSD card, it will be lost if you power off the console. The other "real time save" hotkey lets you save or load a real time save which is similar to a quick save in emulators. Another issue I had with this flash cart is that the hot keys worked in all the GBA variants and in the original DS, but they do not work on DS Lite. If you only have a DS Lite, you cannot save. Period. It reportedly works with the GameCube Gameboy Player, but I did not test this myself.

I'm sure there's a compatibility list somewhere for roms, but I've had a lot of success getting it to run most single player GBA roms. One downside is that whatever video memory the game uses is slightly slower than it should be so there are times where the screen has small glitches due to lag. I noticed this for instance when moving around quickly in Megaman Battle Network 2. I didn't notice any additional battery drain while using it as a GBA cart in both DS and GBA systems.

So, overall verdict... It works, most of the time, in most of the systems, with most games, mostly correct. There are better options available for both GBA and DS roms though, so I recommend you not bother unless you're a homebrew developer who wants to test their creations in as many flash carts and systems as possible.

I'll add any additional links related to the Supercard MiniSD in the comments.

You never know when they'll drop support for a specific flash cart or even when an entire team's site will go away, so I created a backup copy of all the related software for the flash cart, downloaded from the official supercard.sc site on Aug 14, 2015. The most recent software update was in 2010 so I'd expect it to all be final: http://www.mediafire.com/download/iiww38lf8xnpm18/supercard_mini_sd_software.zip

This is a backup of the various "manual" pages from the official site as well. The English is pretty bad but it's better than nothing. Each page was converted to a pdf and then I just lumped the PDF files together for one download: http://www.mediafire.com/download/5bbb64b02afcs3w/supercard_minisd_manual.zip

This video highlights some graphical issues and stuff the flash cart has with certain GBA games, and shows it working with the GameCube: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mW-mfQLolYk

You can also search on YouTube for Supercard Review and you'll find a ton of videos.

It was my birthday this week so my family came to visit and we went out for a meal at a Chinese buffet place. You'll probably know the kind - you pay a flat fee and eat whatever you like. It was fairly quiet when we got there, with only one other family in the whole restaurant. A group of 5 rotund people who looked like a set of bowling ball shaped Russian dolls. They were sat at the table closest to the dessert section. We took our own table and enjoyed our dinner, getting several small tasting plates and trying a bit of everything.

Once we were done with mains we visited the dessert section. This was the only time we were near fat family, and from the looks of their table they'd been there for a while. The dessert cabinet was varied in its choices but nearly empty by this point. While we were debating the mini cheesecakes, the patriarch of the other family waddled over and helped himself to a huge bowl of ice cream from the ice cream machine. I doubt it was his first.

As we sat back at our own table, my dad gave me a nudge. "I bet they're the kind of people of take 'all you can eat' as a challenge."

They were still there when we left and it didn't look like they were slowing down.
